INCORRECT_WORKED_EXAMPLES.name: Spot the Slip
INCORRECT_WORKED_EXAMPLES.subtitle: Locate the breakdown
INCORRECT_WORKED_EXAMPLES.description: Students examine a worked solution, identify the first step where the reasoning goes off track, explain why the step is invalid, and work together to correct the error.

FAVORITE_NO.name: My Favorite No
FAVORITE_NO.subtitle: Preserve and build on productive thinking
FAVORITE_NO.description: Students analyze a meaningful incorrect answer that reveals a mathematical idea worth preserving or building on. They discuss why the response might seem reasonable, identify what the reasoning gets right, and revise it while keeping what is mathematically useful.

MATH_DETECTIVE.name: Math Detective
MATH_DETECTIVE.subtitle: Investigate underlying issues
MATH_DETECTIVE.description: Students become “math detectives” by investigating an incorrect solution, identifying the underlying mathematical issue, revising the reasoning, and checking whether the revision works.

COMPARE_THE_THINKING.name: Compare the Thinking
COMPARE_THE_THINKING.subtitle: Examine meaningful contrasts
COMPARE_THE_THINKING.description: Students compare two meaningfully different solution strategies or representations and examine the reasoning, strengths, limitations, and important mathematical differences between them.
COMPARE_THE_THINKING.artifactTitle: Strategies to compare - Examples to show the class

MAKE_YOUR_CASE.name: Make Your Case
MAKE_YOUR_CASE.subtitle: Articulate and justify claims
MAKE_YOUR_CASE.description: Students make or evaluate a mathematical claim, articulate their thinking, build a case for it using evidence and reasoning, and consider whether the evidence and reasoning support the claim.
MAKE_YOUR_CASE.artifactTitle: The claim - Example to show the class
